postData.contentHtml:
Week 1 of the fantasy football season often throws curveballs, and this year was no exception, especially at the tight end position. Unexpected breakouts and quiet performances have left many managers re-evaluating their strategies for Week 2. To help you navigate the ever-changing landscape, we've analyzed the latest rankings, injury reports, and expert insights to identify who to start, who to sit, and the top sleepers to consider.

Risers After Week 1 Surprises

Several tight ends made a strong case for increased attention after their Week 1 showings. Trey McBride led the pack with a heavy workload, securing nine catches for 95 yards on 13 targets, firmly establishing himself as a top option. Dalton Kincaid also saw a significant boost, converting six targets into five receptions for an impressive 130 yards. Not to be outdone, Isaiah Likely showcased his red-zone prowess with eight catches, 78 yards, and two touchdowns, keeping him firmly in the weekly TE1 conversation. These performances suggest a shift in the tight end hierarchy, and managers should adjust their expectations accordingly.

Injury Watch: The Brock Bowers Effect and Michael Mayer's Opportunity

The injury status of Brock Bowers remains a critical factor for Week 2. Having missed Week 1 due to a knee injury, his return would undoubtedly place him among the top tight ends. However, if Bowers remains sidelined, Michael Mayer of the Las Vegas Raiders emerges as a prime streaming option. In Week 1, Mayer was heavily involved, leading the Raiders with seven targets and running 23 routes. His Week 2 matchup against the Chargers, a team that recently allowed Trey McBride to put up 24.5 fantasy points, makes Mayer an especially attractive play if Bowers is out. Stay tuned for the latest updates on Bowers' health.

Proceed with Caution: Kyle Pitts' Week 2 Outlook

On the other end of the spectrum, Kyle Pitts presents a challenging decision for fantasy managers. After an extremely quiet Week 1 where he saw only one target and finished with zero fantasy points despite running 21 routes, trust in Pitts is waning. Atlanta's uncertain quarterback situation further complicates his outlook, making him a risky Week 2 start even with a seemingly favorable matchup against Carolina. Consider other options if you have them.

Beyond the Rankings: Matchups and Momentum

While individual player performances are key, understanding matchups and team dynamics is equally important. Experts are delving into favorable and unfavorable matchups across all positions, with tight ends being no exception. The generally positive sentiment among the fantasy football community, coupled with active debates on social media, underscores the dynamic nature of Week 2 decisions. Stay informed, consult multiple sources, and trust your gut to make the best lineup choices.
postData.title: Week 2 Fantasy Football Tight End Rankings: Who to Start, Who to Sit, and Key Sleepers
postData.summary: After a surprising Week 1, fantasy football managers are scrambling to optimize their tight end lineups for Week 2. Get the latest insights on top performers, injury impacts, and potential sleepers to give you the edge.
